reviews.head: 70d78e27df7ade59f5a240f892d65dd9b48dfbda
verified: Read complete ocr_queue.py and all changed tests/docs/product fragment; inspected text submission, task status and lifecycle callers using exact source fallback.

Each persistent page reserves its own attempt before _run_unit; final assembly uses separate sentinel -1 before assembly/response/write. SQLite conditional UPSERT caps attempts atomically at three; terminal jobs cannot reserve another unit.

Checkpoint write and corresponding attempt deletion are one transaction. Recovery loads completed units and schedules only missing units, preserving page order and original work. Third attempt can succeed.

Exhaustion becomes terminal failed through existing error path, clears pending units, releases active slot, deletes input/checkpoints/attempts and preserves terminal error across restart. Subsequent work completes.
Additive IF NOT EXISTS attempt table upgrades an older ledger without rewriting checkpoints. Startup/sweeper clear orphan attempts; synchronous in-memory operations do not use persistent budgets.

README accurately scopes this to repeated persistent-work interruptions, including abandoned shutdown work; it does not claim live inference timeout or determine OOM cause. No configuration/worker-count changes.

independent_focused_tests.coverage: Real child-process SIGKILL page/assembly exhaustion; checkpoint reuse; third page attempt success; terminal persistence and cleanup; following-job completion; atomic rollback; legacy ledger upgrade.

results: 16 concurrent reservations: exactly 3 accepted, 13 rejected; separate page/assembly counters preserved; terminal row rejects new work.
After two actual SIGKILL interruptions during assembly, third assembly succeeds using all three recorded page checkpoints without rerunning them; following job completes and attempt rows are empty.

limitations: Only local synthetic inputs and isolated temporary ledgers were used; no customer data, production mutations, source edits or remote actions.
Tests exercise process SIGKILL, not actual model inference/OOM or host power loss; existing SQLite WAL NORMAL policy remains unchanged.
Persistent page/assembly restart budget does not bound live inference duration, startup decoding work or synchronous orientation/table operation retries.
No deployment, capacity or financial extraction accuracy claim.
Graph unavailable per parent; direct exact-source review used without a graph-completeness claim.

reviews.verdictMeaning: Not CLEAN: reproducible compatibility/concurrency regression. This label follows the requested verdict vocabulary and does not allege intentional evidence manipulation.

findings.title: Repeated requested page indices exhaust the new budget without interruptions
findings.reproduction: Start actual queue with4 workers and1 active slot, submit a one-page native PDF with pages=[0,0,0,0]. Hold the first three read entries long enough for all workers to start, then release and execute the original native reader/assembler. Base7a0a68f completes and returns4 pages; candidate70d78e27 fails OCR page1 could not finish after3 attempts although no process or read was interrupted.
findings.cause: OcrRequest, rapid_ocr.plan and _validate_pages accept duplicate indices. _Job.units schedules each duplicate, but ocr_job_attempts keys only by(job_id, physical page index). Simultaneous legitimate starts are mistaken for retries.
findings.suggestedFix: Schedule each physical page index only once for persistent jobs, preserving original job.targets order and multiplicity for assembly. Apply the same unique scheduling invariant during recovery; keep in-memory operation behavior intentional. Add duplicate-index concurrency and recovery regressions.

positiveChecks: Reviewed complete changed runtime file and changed tests/docs, with exact source fallback after graph unavailable.

Attempt UPSERT is atomic under SQLite locking and occurs before work; checkpoint insertion and page-counter deletion are one transaction. Assembly counter is independent. Terminal cleanup and orphan attempt sweeping preserve prior contracts.

Independent actual native-PDF SIGKILL after checkpoint commit: page0 persisted and counter removed atomically; new process executed only pages1,2 and returned exactly[0,1,2] with complete_pages3. No fake inference or assembly used in this probe.

Committed tests use actual subprocess SIGKILL and actual encrypted queue persistence with explicitly substituted inference/assembly; those tests are suitable for queue interruption boundaries but miss duplicate requested page indices.
Inspected parent215/215 tests and checker5/5 test evidence; these passes do not cover the reproduced regression.

duplicatePages.error: OCR page 1 could not finish after 3 attempts; processing stopped after repeated interruptions

checkpointBoundary.inference: Actual native PDF read and actual assembly; no fake inference/results.

limitations: One-process scheduler contract WORKERS=1; multi-process ownership/leases are outside scope.
Process-interruption budget does not bound live inference duration, model memory consumption, host power loss or startup decoding. Existing WAL NORMAL policy unchanged.
No real OCR model/OOM or deployment/capacity/accuracy claim. Probes use only generated native PDFs and private temporary ledgers.
Reviewer made no repository source edits, production actions or remote writes.

reviews.head: 884fcf2580e3e8b7ed3cf1a12f4b3d85ed8109a9
verified: Only _Job.units scheduling changes: dict.fromkeys preserves first-appearance order and schedules every physical page once, excluding already checkpointed pages. Original targets remain unchanged.
One page therefore cannot consume multiple persistent attempts merely because it occurs repeatedly in a request. Existing attempt budgets and checkpoint cleanup remain unchanged.

RapidOCR _assemble reconstructs results from job.done in original targets order, including repeated entries. rapid_ocr.assemble copies result dictionaries and retains ordered response pages and multiplicity. Existing searchable-PDF handling is unchanged.

The common _Job change also deduplicates synchronous page work; its output still follows original targets. An independent direct probe verifies a checkpointed page is omitted from work while repeated output remains intact.

New native PDF regressions test fresh and recovered jobs with four workers and six requested entries for two physical pages; recovery starts with two attempts already spent. Both complete with each physical page read once.

prior_review.retained_scope: Round1 attempt accounting, terminal failure, cleanup and legacy ledger review; amended here for duplicate-page scheduling.

limitations: No source edits, remote operations, customer data or production mutations.
Local native synthetic PDFs and fake-inference SIGKILL tests; no actual model OOM, production qualification or deployment claim.

resolved.resolution: Pending units now deduplicate physical page indices in first-occurrence order while targets keeps the requested sequence and multiplicity. Fresh and recovered jobs share that invariant, so concurrent duplicate entries cannot spend the same unfinished-page retry budget.

checks: Read exact two-file delta: _Job.units uniqueness plus fresh/recovery duplicate-page tests; no changes to counter transaction, checkpoint storage, assembly ordering or result-status logic.

Independent original accepted-request replay: base and candidate both return4 pages for[0,0,0,0]; candidate now runs physical page0 exactly once and completes without retry exhaustion. Actual native reader and assembler used.

Independent fresh-process recovery: page0 already checkpointed, page1 attempts=2, requested targets[1,0,1,1,0]. Recovery reads only page1 once, succeeds on its third attempt, returns exact sequence, coverage complete_pages5 and no remaining attempt rows.
Parent round2-tests.log independently inspected:217 passed, one unrelated Starlette/httpx deprecation warning. Broad suite not duplicated.
Prior bounded review of atomic counters, checkpoint commit, SIGKILL recovery, terminal failure/progression and compatibility remains applicable. Historical round1 receipt preserved.

recoveryDuplicates.execution: Fresh subprocess, actual native PDF reader/assembly. One physical page checkpoint preserved; other page succeeds on its third permitted attempt.

limitations: Bounded restart and concurrency review only; no live inference timeout, real-model OOM, host power-loss, capacity or production-deployment claim.
Single process scheduler ownership remains required; independent multi-process queue scheduling is outside scope.
Physical-unit deduplication also applies to queued in-memory page jobs; original targets preserve output multiplicity and order.
No repository source edits or production actions; generated native PDF probes and temporary local ledgers only.
